clue.text: Ambiguous language when information is brought to summit

parts.note: news is information about recent events
a peak is a summit

explanation.surface: A complaint that waffly language takes over whenever news reaches a summit meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWSPEAK is the deliberately evasive official language of Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's coinage is now used for any slippery official jargon designed to mislead.

clue.text: Appropriate score

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to take for oneself, to steal
a notch or cut, as scored in wood

explanation.definitionFit: Nick is slang for steal and also means a small cut or notch.

clue.text: My word!.It's spring

definitions.meaning: a spring is a natural water source

explanation.definitionFit: Well is an exclamation of surprise, and a well is a source of water like a spring.

clue.text: Demure over sex appeal, I have to be crude

indicators.note: over says the demure piece sits above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: prim means demure
it is old slang for sex appeal
I've contracts I have

explanation.surface: A demure person with sex appeal confesses to being crude.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means simple and unsophisticated, roughly made.

clue.text: Pa hit 'ma there — dreadful scene of conflict

indicators.note: dreadful hints at a mess, so the letters of the phrase before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A domestic fight: Dad hit Mum there, a dreadful scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena where gladiators fought is a place of combat.

clue.text: Class one consultant initially holds in hospital

indicators.note: holds means the run of letters before it grips another piece inside

parts.note: CL is a standard abbreviation for class
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word consultant

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A top-grade consultant doing a session at a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a medical establishment, often attached to or part of a hospital, where patients are seen.

clue.text: Religious symbol conveys fate to you and me

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A religious emblem that carries a message of destiny to us.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus flower is a sacred emblem in Hinduism and Buddhism.

clue.text: Like ice-cream on plate Ian demolished

indicators.note: demolished means the letters before it are knocked down and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Ian wolfed down the ice-cream on his plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolished' reads as 'ate up', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Neapolitan ice-cream has layered bands of different flavours.

clue.text: Awful scares about old cattle showing frailty

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the next piece
awful means the letters of scares are badly jumbled

parts.note: kine is an archaic plural of cow

explanation.surface: Dreadful frights involving old cows show their weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' looks like part of the surface's judgement of the scares, but it signals the anagram; KINE is an old word solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Creaking with age suggests weakness and infirmity.

clue.text: Muse about everything that is about work

parts.note: C, from Latin circa, is short for about
all means everything

indicators.note: about here means the letters for 'that is' go round the next piece

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A muse who is concerned with everything to do with work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' appears twice with two jobs: first as the abbreviation circa, then as a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, presiding over epic poetry.

clue.text: Gas from English aristocrat of yesteryear

parts.note: a thane was a nobleman in Anglo-Saxon England and old Scotland

explanation.surface: A remark that hot air comes from an old English nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethane is a colourless hydrocarbon gas found in natural gas.

clue.text: Classical, problem that could land Romans in soup

indicators.note: could land suggests the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tough classical puzzle that might get the Romans into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In soup' is part of the fodder, though it reads as 'in trouble'. The Latin phrase, 'bridge of asses', names Euclid's theorem on isosceles triangles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag for a classic geometrical theorem that tests weak students.

clue.text: One may be resigned when caller comes back

definitions.text: One may be resigned when caller comes back

parts.words: One may be resigned when caller comes back
parts.note: resigned reads as re-signed: a returning guest writes their name in it once more

explanation.surface: Someone resigned to the return of an unwanted caller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resigned' looks like 'accepting one's fate', but is to be read as 'signed again'.
explanation.definitionFit: Guests at a house, museum or hotel sign this register when they visit.

clue.text: Extremely pale-looking entertainer rests in car

indicators.note: in says the entertainer and rests pieces sit inside the car

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a type of car
a host entertains guests
lies means rests

explanation.surface: A very pale entertainer lies back in a sports car.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of ghostly describes the palest, most spectral appearance.

clue.text: Question master in panel game, we hear — one coming to a peak

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: we hear means a word heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: a quiz is a game for a panel of contestants
the Roman numeral for one is I
a tor is a rocky peak

explanation.surface: A quizmaster on a TV panel game introducing a climber reaching a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand inquisitor interrogated suspected heretics, asking the questions.

clue.text: Language rich in dialect to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A language that is rich in regional dialects.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is a major tongue of northern India, one of its official languages.

clue.text: Is Iran hot, possibly? I'm no geographer!

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of the words before it could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether Iran is hot pleads that geography is not their subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the speaker's protest: a scholar of the past rather than of places.
explanation.definitionFit: A student of history is a different specialist from someone who studies places and climates.

clue.text: Alert, not drunk — the man before dance

indicators.note: before says the man piece comes ahead of the dance piece
drunk means the letters of not are rearranged, staggering

parts.note: he refers to the man
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone sober and alert before a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sharp and quick to react means being wide awake.

clue.text: Kitchen utensils break around lip to start with

indicators.note: to start with says the cheek piece goes first

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, as is sauce

indicators.note: around means the word for break is turned back to front

parts.note: to snap is to break

explanation.surface: Advice to break the lip of a pan as a first step in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Pans with handles used for boiling and stewing on the hob are basic cookware.

clue.text: Vehicles may be brisk making: return journey

indicators.note: a return journey goes back the way it came, so the word for brisk is read in the other direction

parts.note: smart means brisk, as in a smart pace

explanation.surface: Vehicles that might be quick on the way home.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are passenger vehicles running on rails along city streets.

clue.text: Office equipment that's errant fixed with pliers

indicators.note: fixed suggests the letters have been mended into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wayward office machine repaired with a pair of pliers.
explanation.definitionFit: This desktop device prints documents using a laser beam and toner.

clue.text: Quarrel draws any number into destruction

indicators.note: into means the number piece goes inside the destruction piece

parts.note: ruin is destruction
N stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: A quarrel brings any number of people to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is an argument or clash with someone.

clue.text: Renounce study to get ultimate in luxury

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room

indicators.note: ultimate in means take the final letter of luxury

explanation.surface: Give up studying to enjoy the height of luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny something is to disown or reject it.

clue.text: Celebrity makes one goggle no end

indicators.note: no end means the last letter is taken off

parts.note: to stare is to goggle

explanation.surface: A celebrity who makes people gawp endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer.

clue.text: Space no longer given' to shelter

parts.note: ex means former, something no longer given or held
a tent is a shelter

explanation.surface: A space no longer offered as somewhere to camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent means the area or size that something covers.

clue.text: Embellish holy books with gold label at front

indicators.note: at front says the gold and label pieces come before the holy books

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a name is a label
NT is the New Testament, a set of holy books

explanation.surface: An instruction to decorate scripture with a gilded title page.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to decorate or adorn.

clue.text: Chair being chucked in speech :

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: chucked means thrown

explanation.surface: A chair being flung across the room during an address.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne is the ceremonial seat of a monarch or bishop.

clue.text: Boss has backed me — strategy coming with little hesitation

indicators.note: backed means the word me is written from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a ploy is a strategy
er is the small noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A boss supported me, though with a little hesitation over strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who gives you a job and pays your wages is your boss.
